1.0.0.en: 1 Now it came to pass in the days of Ahasuerus, (this is Ahasuerus which reigned, from India even unto Ethiopia, over an hundred and seven and twenty provinces:) 2 That in those days, when the king Ahasuerus sat on the throne of his kingdom, which was in Shushan the palace, 3 In the third year of his reign, he made a feast unto all his princes and his servants; the power of Persia and Media, the nobles and princes of the provinces, being before him: 4 When he shewed the riches of his glorious kingdom and the honour of his excellent majesty many days, even an hundred and fourscore days. 5 And when these days were expired, the king made a feast unto all the people that were present in Shushan the palace, both unto great and small, seven days, in the court of the garden of the king’s palace; 6 Where were white, green, and blue, hangings, fastened with cords of fine linen and purple to silver rings and pillars of marble: the beds were of gold and silver, upon a pavement of alabaster, and marble, and pearl, and black marble. 7 And they gave them drink in vessels of gold, (the vessels being diverse one from another,) and royal wine in abundance, according to the state of the king. 8 And the drinking was according to the law; none did compel: for so the king had appointed to all the officers of his house, that they should do according to every man’s pleasure. 9 Also Vashti the queen made a feast for the women in the royal house which belonged to king Ahasuerus.

1.0.1.en: The kingdom of Media and Persia grew great and defeated the kingdom of Babylon, so the Jews who had been carried captive to Babylon came under Persian rule. The extent of this kingdom reached the point that it contained 127 provinces (states) stretching from India to Cush [1], that is, to Nubia and Kordofan, south of Egypt and north of Ethiopia. Among these provinces was the province of Egypt, which the emperor Xerxes occupied after his father had failed to seize it.

1.0.2.en: We have said that Ahasuerus [1] means King Xerxes the son of Darius. Since more than one king was given the title Ahasuerus, some scholars see that this word does not signify the king’s name but is a title special to the kings of Persia, like saying “Pharaoh” of the king of Egypt.

1.1.0.en: The king wanted to show the riches of the glory of his kingdom and the honour of the splendor of his majesty [4], so he made two great feasts. The first lasted 180 days; perhaps he held a daily feast for each province separately, together with special feasts for the princes as a body, or perhaps these cities covered the long period of preparing the two feasts. As for the second feast, [it was held for all the people, from great to small, a feast of seven days in the court of the garden of the king’s palace] [5].

1.1.1.en: Perhaps he prepared these two feasts in order to devise the plan of war against Greece, for Herodotus says that the Persians were accustomed to take their decisions at such feasts.

1.2.0.en: The book describes the feast in precise detail, mentioning that it was held in Shushan the palace. “Shushan,” or “Susa,” has been the capital of Elam since about the year 3000 B.C.; it was the seat of King Chedorlaomer (Gen 14:1). The kings of Media and Persia took possession of it and made it a capital alongside Babylon and Ecbatana, and the kings preferred to stay in it, especially in the winter. The first feast, for the princes, was apparently held inside the palace. The second, which included all the people residing in the palace and its dependencies (it seems it was separate from the city itself (Esth 9:12-13)), was held in the garden of the palace, where there were hangings (fabrics) of white, green and blue, which are the royal colors in Persia. These hangings were fastened with cords of fine linen (white linen) and purple to rings of silver and pillars of marble; the hangings were used for protection from the heat of the sun. The beds were inlaid with gold and silver upon a pavement, that is, a floor of tiles, of alabaster (a white stone that gleams), marble, pearl and black marble. The most notable feature of the feast was the drinking of the royal wine, which was found in abundance “according to the state of the king” [7], but he left the freedom of drinking to the choice of each person.

1.2.1.en: At the time when the king held this feast, the queen also held a feast for the women in the king’s house.

1.3.0.en: 10 On the seventh day, when the heart of the king was merry with wine, he commanded Mehuman, Biztha, Harbona, Bigtha, and Abagtha, Zethar, and Carcas, the seven chamberlains that served in the presence of Ahasuerus the king, 11 To bring Vashti the queen before the king with the crown royal, to shew the people and the princes her beauty: for she was fair to look on. 12 But the queen Vashti refused to come at the king’s commandment by his chamberlains: therefore was the king very wroth, and his anger burned in him.

1.3.1.en: “On the seventh day, when the heart of the king was merry with wine, he commanded Mehuman, Biztha, Harbona, Bigtha, and Abagtha, Zethar, and Carcas, the seven chamberlains that served in the presence of Ahasuerus the king, to bring Vashti the queen before the king with the crown royal, to shew the people and the princes her beauty: for she was fair to look on” [10-11].

1.3.2.en: The king’s heart was merry with wine, so he lost his balance, and in foolishness he asked his seven chamberlains to bring the queen so that her beauty might be shown to the peoples and the princes. Here the word “eunuch” (chamberlain) does not carry its literal meaning, that is, a castrated man, but is a title that was given to the holders of royal offices in Egypt and Persia. Potiphar, the captain of the guard, was called “an officer of Pharaoh” (Gen 39:1), and so were the chief of Pharaoh’s cupbearers and his chief baker (Gen 40:2)... So the seven chamberlains are the men entrusted with the royal affairs, and they enjoy the favor of servants before the king.

1.3.3.en: The king’s heart was merry with wine, so he uttered perverse things, as the wise man says: “Look not thou upon the wine when it is red, when it giveth his colour in the cup, when it moveth itself aright. At the last it biteth like a serpent, and stingeth like an adder... thine heart shall utter perverse things” (Prov 23:31-33); “It is not for kings... to drink wine; nor for princes strong drink: lest they drink, and forget the law, and pervert the judgment of any of the afflicted” (Prov 31:4-5).

1.3.4.en: If in Christ Jesus we have become kings (Rev 1:6; 5:10), it is not fitting for us to become drunk with the wine of the love of this world and its pleasures, lest we forget the law of heaven and lose our fitting royal work, and demand the inner “Vashti” so that she may show her beauty before the peoples and the princes, that is, we present works of righteousness and virtues to gain human glory and for outward show, instead of our queen being within us, revealing her beauty only to her Bridegroom, our Lord Jesus!

1.3.5.en: If God has set man up as a spiritual king, then it is fitting for him not to demand his wife the queen in order to display her beauty, but to keep her in the house of the women, holding the feast for the women, so that they rejoice in her and submit to her. In other words, let our bodies (the wife) remain subject to the soul (the king), hidden in their royal conduct, living in a spirit of submission to the soul so as to remain holy in the Lord, sharing with the soul her glory and royal dignity. The Apostle Paul loved “Vashti,” that is, his royal body in the Lord, and left her in the house of the women, when he said: [I keep under my body, and bring it into subjection: lest that by any means, when I have preached to others, I myself should be a castaway] (1 Cor 9:27), “For no man ever yet hated his own flesh; but nourisheth and cherisheth it, even as the Lord the church,” that is, as a king toward the queen. Let the soul know its leading position by the Holy Spirit, and let the body know its position as a helper to the soul and a partner with her in victory, and the whole man is deprived of the eternal royal glory.

1.3.6.en: The king wanted to bring out the beauty of the queen “for she was fair to look on,” and he did not realize that by displaying her beauty she loses her dignity and her image is disfigured. For this reason our Lord Jesus affirmed our obligation not to display our inner queen, when He says: “Let not thy left hand know what thy right hand doeth: that thine alms may be in secret: and thy Father which seeth in secret himself shall reward thee openly” (Mt 6:3-4). Vashti remains in the house of the women when we offer worship to God not with the intent of appearing before people but by closing our inner doors and entering into the secret place, where we meet our unseen Bridegroom. As St. John Chrysostom says: [God Himself is unseen, therefore He wishes your prayer also to be unseen], and he also says: [God desires that the doors of the mind be shut rather than the (visible) doors].

1.4.s.en: 3. Taking the kingdom away from Vashti:

1.4.0.en: 13 Then the king said to the wise men, which knew the times, (for so was the king’s manner toward all that knew law and judgment: 14 And the next unto him were Carshena, Shethar, Admatha, Tarshish, Meres, Marsena, and Memucan, the seven princes of Persia and Media, which saw the king’s face, and which sat the first in the kingdom;) 15 “What shall we do unto the queen Vashti according to law, because she hath not performed the commandment of the king Ahasuerus by the chamberlains?” 16 And Memucan answered before the king and the princes, “Vashti the queen hath not done wrong to the king only, but also to all the princes, and to all the people that are in all the provinces of the king Ahasuerus. 17 For this deed of the queen shall come abroad unto all women, so that they shall despise their husbands in their eyes, when it shall be reported, The king Ahasuerus commanded Vashti the queen to be brought in before him, but she came not. 18 Likewise shall the ladies of Persia and Media say this day unto all the king’s princes, which have heard of the deed of the queen. Thus shall there arise too much contempt and wrath. 19 If it please the king, let there go a royal commandment from him, and let it be written among the laws of the Persians and the Medes, that it be not altered, That Vashti come no more before king Ahasuerus; and let the king give her royal estate unto another that is better than she. 20 And when the king’s decree which he shall make shall be published throughout all his empire, (for it is great,) all the wives shall give to their husbands honour, both to great and small.” 21 And the saying pleased the king and the princes; and the king did according to the word of Memucan: 22 For he sent letters into all the king’s provinces, into every province according to the writing thereof, and to every people after their language, that every man should bear rule in his own house, and that it should be published according to the language of every people.

1.4.1.en: When the queen refused to come, “the king was very wroth, and his anger burned in him” [12], and thus he turned to the opposite, from intense love and admiration for his wife the queen to flames of anger burning in him against her.

1.4.2.en: The king consulted the wise men who knew the times (perhaps meaning magicians and diviners) [13], and those who knew law and judgment... And since there seem to have been differences between the queen and Memucan, one of these counselors of the king, he exaggerated the matter and counted what Vashti had done as a wrong not only against the king and the princes but against all the men of his kingdom, for when the women hear what happened they will despise their husbands. And he asked that the kingdom be taken away from her and given to one who is better than she [19].

1.4.3.en: Memucan counted Vashti’s conduct as a breach of the law of nature and the law of the family, whereby the man loses his authority over his wife and the wife despises her husband, and he thought that it is laws that support the man and give him authority. Perhaps this conduct reveals an inner feeling that was passing through the lives of men in that age, namely the inability to control and lead the family; they did not realize that wise leadership does not draw its strength from laws and commands but from a spirit of self-giving love, as the Apostle says: “Husbands, love your wives, even as Christ also loved the church, and gave himself for it... Nevertheless let every one of you in particular so love his wife even as himself” (Eph 5:25, 33).

1.5.0.en: Memucan says: “that every man should bear rule in his own house, and that it should be published according to the language of every people” [22], meaning that if a man marries a woman of another race, the household is obliged to speak the language of the man and not the woman. This is the picture of family life in the minds of the men of Persia, and they did not realize that the language that prevails in the home must be the language of love, which is able to captivate the beloved. Between wife and husband there is no struggle for authority; rather there ought to be between them a longing for self-giving that works through inner love, and an awareness of the unity of life and thought.

1.5.1.en: Ahasuerus loved Vashti for her beauty, her lineage and her wealth, and in his anger he took counsel with others about her. We, however, receive the wife (or the husband) from the hand of God, that He may grant us the spirit of unity in Him, sanctifying the family relationship which cannot be dissolved. As Tertullian says: [How can I describe the happiness of the marriage that the Church approves, the offering confirms, the blessing seals, the angels announce, and the Father declares lawful?!].

2.0.s.en: 1. The need for a new queen:

2.0.0.en: 1 After these things, when the wrath of king Ahasuerus was appeased, he remembered Vashti, and what she had done, and what was decreed against her. 2 Then said the king’s servants that ministered unto him, “Let there be fair young virgins sought for the king: 3 And let the king appoint officers in all the provinces of his kingdom, that they may gather together all the fair young virgins unto Shushan the palace, to the house of the women, unto the custody of Hege the king’s chamberlain, keeper of the women; and let their things for purification be given them: 4 And let the maiden which pleaseth the king be queen instead of Vashti.” And the thing pleased the king; and he did so.

2.0.1.en: “After these things, when the wrath of king Ahasuerus was appeased, he remembered Vashti, and what she had done, and what was decreed against her. Then said the king’s servants that ministered unto him, Let there be fair young virgins sought for the king: and let the king appoint officers in all the provinces of his kingdom, that they may gather together all the fair young virgins unto Shushan the palace, to the house of the women, unto the custody of Hege the king’s chamberlain, keeper of the women; and let their things for purification be given them: and let the maiden which pleaseth the king be queen instead of Vashti” [1-3].

2.0.2.en: The king’s wrath was appeased and he remembered Vashti, and perhaps he could have pardoned her, but the counselors feared lest she take vengeance on them because of their counsel to the king, so they hastened to urge him to choose a beautiful wife. It is said that the king used to choose his wife from the daughters of the princes, but since the men feared that the king would think they had pushed him to dismiss Vashti for a personal interest, they tried to show their good intention by having the king choose the beautiful maiden from any province or any race, as they would gather for him the fair maidens from the whole kingdom. By this they wanted to offer a remedy for the dismissal of Vashti by installing a beautiful woman in her place. As St. Jerome says: [The philosophers of the world used to remove an old passion by instilling a new passion, driving out one nail by fixing another. On this basis the seven princes of Persia acted with King Ahasuerus, for they removed his regret over Vashti the queen by stirring up in him love for other virgins. They heal one fault with another, and one sin with another sin; but for us it is fitting to overcome our faults by teaching ourselves the love of the opposite virtues. As the psalmist says: “Depart from evil, and do good; seek peace, and pursue it” (Ps 34:14). For if we do not hate evil we cannot love good; rather let us do good if we wish to leave evil; let us seek peace if we wish to avoid war.]

2.0.3.en: The princes exploited the weakness of the king’s character and his love of licentiousness, so they quenched his longing for Vashti by offering beautiful maidens to the house of the women, that he might choose according to his desire.

2.0.4.en: If we take the symbolic or spiritual interpretation, we ask: who are these servants who minister to him and ask him to set up a new queen instead of Vashti, if not the men of faith of the Old Testament, patriarchs, prophets, kings, priests and laymen, who lived under the shadow of the Law (Vashti), and realized that there is no salvation for them by the Law, especially in its literalness, since “the commandment (the Law), which was ordained to life, I found to be unto death. For sin, taking occasion by the commandment, deceived me, and by it slew me” (Rom 7:10-11). The Law exposed sin and disgraced it (Rom 7:12) and confirmed the death of man instead of supporting, healing and saving him. For this reason the men of the Old Testament awaited with joy the coming of the “Messiah,” the Savior, to set up Esther as queen through the free grace of the Gospel, as the Lord Himself says: “Your father Abraham rejoiced to see my day: and he saw it, and was glad” (Jn 8:56).

2.0.5.en: The servants asked that the fair young virgins be gathered from the whole kingdom to Shushan the palace, as if they, the men of the Old Testament, saw the Church of the New Testament, which has included in its membership children from all the nations and peoples, and has entered with them into the house of the virgins in the palace of Christ, that is, the Church which is called “the church of the firstborn” (Heb 12:23), to declare her spiritual virginity and her inner beauty as “a glorious church, not having spot, or wrinkle, or any such thing; but that it should be holy and without blemish” (Eph 5:27). The believers longed to see this holy virgin as a bride for the King, as the Apostle Paul says: “For I have espoused you to one husband, that I may present you as a chaste virgin to Christ” (2 Cor 11:2).

2.1.0.en: 5 Now in Shushan the palace there was a certain Jew, whose name was Mordecai, the son of Jair, the son of Shimei, the son of Kish, a Benjamite; 6 Who had been carried away from Jerusalem with the captivity which had been carried away with Jeconiah king of Judah, whom Nebuchadnezzar the king of Babylon had carried away. 7 And he brought up Hadassah, that is, Esther, his uncle’s daughter: for she had neither father nor mother, and the maid was fair and beautiful; whom Mordecai, when her father and mother were dead, took for his own daughter. 8 So it came to pass, when the king’s commandment and his decree was heard, and when many maidens were gathered together unto Shushan the palace, to the custody of Hegai, that Esther was brought also unto the king’s house, to the custody of Hegai, keeper of the women. 9 And the maiden pleased him, and she obtained kindness of him; and he speedily gave her her things for purification, with such things as belonged to her, and seven maidens, which were meet to be given her, out of the king’s house: and he preferred her and her maids unto the best place of the house of the women. 10 Esther had not shewed her people nor her kindred: for Mordecai had charged her that she should not shew it. 11 And Mordecai walked every day before the court of the women’s house, to know how Esther did, and what should become of her.

2.1.1.en: When Vashti was removed from the kingdom, God turned this matter to the salvation of His people by raising up Esther, who was born in the land of captivity and was brought up by her cousin Mordecai, as queen instead of Vashti.

2.1.2.en: The book speaks of Mordecai, who worked in Shushan the palace; he was a Jew carried away from Jerusalem in the days of Jeconiah king of Judah by Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon. What draws our attention is that the hidden hero in the story of Esther is “Mordecai,” who was marked by faithfulness in raising Esther and in his guidance to her, and by faithfulness in his work for the king, who was of a foreign race, saving his life from a wicked plot; he was also distinguished by a deeply spiritual conduct filled with faith and trust in the work of God.

2.1.3.en: We have said that Vashti signifies the literalness of the Law, which must be removed from the heart so that the grace of the New Testament may reign, and Esther (the Church of the New Testament) appears as queen. The features and circumstances of Esther came in conformity with the Church of the New Testament in many respects, of which we mention:

2.1.4.en: First: Esther was born in the land of captivity, deprived of the Promised Land and of the Temple with all its beautiful rituals, as if she represents the company of the Gentiles who fell under the captivity of the devil, deprived of God’s spiritual blessings and of the enjoyment of His temple... But God raised them from this captivity and made them spiritual kings, for the Lord Christ came to set them free, as it is said by Isaiah: “He hath sent me to bind up the brokenhearted, to proclaim liberty to the captives, and the opening of the prison to them that are bound” (Isa 61:1).

2.1.5.en: St. Augustine says: [Our captivity was removed, not by our being freed from the hands of the barbarians... but from our evil works and from our sins by which the devil had dominion over us; whoever is freed from his sins, the chief of sinners (the devil) no longer has dominion over him], and he also says: [Confess that you are a captive and you will deserve to be freed; for he who does not know his enemy, how can he urge on his deliverer?].

2.2.0.en: Second: “she had neither father nor mother” [7], that is, she was an orphan. This is the mark of the Church when she fulfilled God’s call to Abraham: “Get thee... from thy father’s house” (Gen 12:1). Let us leave our old father, the devil, and our first mother, that is, the love of the world, so that the Lord Himself may be our heavenly Father and the heavenly Church our mother. The Lord asked the Jews to become orphans of their evil father when He said to them: “Ye are of your father the devil, and the lusts of your father ye will do” (Jn 8:44). And St. Augustine speaks about the Gentiles’ leaving their old father, saying: [The Gentiles came from their father Satan and renounced their sonship to him].

2.2.1.en: Third: “the maid was fair and beautiful” [7]... The heavenly Bridegroom sees in His bride the queen a beauty that He Himself poured upon her, for He says to her: “And thy renown went forth among the heathen for thy beauty: for it was perfect through my comeliness, which I had put upon thee, saith the Lord GOD” (Ezek 16:14). Though our past was disgraced by the blackness of sin, yet with exultation we say: “I am black, but comely, O ye daughters of Jerusalem” (Song 1:5). And as St. Ambrose says: [Since you put on those garments through the font of Baptism, you say in the Song of Songs, “I am black, but comely (perfect), O ye daughters of Jerusalem.” I am black through human weakness, perfect through the mystery of faith].

2.3.0.en: Fourth: “(Hegai) moved her with her maids to the best place in the house of the women, and Esther did not tell of her people and her kindred” [9-10].

2.4.0.en: Hegai was the keeper of the house of the virgins, and Shaashgaz the keeper of the concubines [14]. As for Esther, she entered the house of the virgins and was placed in the best place in it, for he realized that she would find favour in the sight of the king and be made queen. What is this place if not “sonship to God,” which became ours as the gift of the Holy Spirit to us in Christ Jesus, the only-begotten Son? For in Him we have been raised into the bosom of His Father, to be found with Him as sons of His.

2.4.1.en: Esther did not tell of her people and her kindred, as Mordecai counseled. For the soul, when it enjoys sonship to God and becomes a queen, lives on a heavenly level, and it has a transcendent race that language cannot express. She lives in silence, not the silence of helplessness grounded in the closing of the heart, but the silence of love opened toward heaven, contemplating the works of God with a glorious joy that cannot be spoken.

2.5.0.en: Fifth: her humility. Esther was marked by a spirit of obedience and submission to her foster father Mordecai even after she sat as queen on the greatest throne of that time, for it is said: “for Esther did the commandment of Mordecai, like as when she was brought up with him” [20].

2.6.0.en: 12 Now when every maid’s turn was come to go in to king Ahasuerus, after that she had been twelve months, according to the manner of the women, (for so were the days of their purifications accomplished, to wit, six months with oil of myrrh, and six months with sweet odours, and with other things for the purifying of the women;) 13 Then thus came every maiden unto the king; whatsoever she desired was given her to go with her out of the house of the women unto the king’s house. 14 In the evening she went, and on the morrow she returned into the second house of the women, to the custody of Shaashgaz, the king’s chamberlain, which kept the concubines: she came in unto the king no more, except the king delighted in her, and that she were called by name. 15 Now when the turn of Esther, the daughter of Abihail the uncle of Mordecai, who had taken her for his daughter, was come to go in unto the king, she required nothing but what Hegai the king’s chamberlain, the keeper of the women, appointed. And Esther obtained favour in the sight of all them that looked upon her. 16 So Esther was taken unto king Ahasuerus into his house royal in the tenth month, which is the month Tebeth, in the seventh year of his reign. 17 And the king loved Esther above all the women, and she obtained grace and favour in his sight more than all the virgins; so that he set the royal crown upon her head, and made her queen instead of Vashti. 18 Then the king made a great feast unto all his princes and his servants, even Esther’s feast; and he made a release to the provinces, and gave gifts, according to the state of the king. 19 And when the virgins were gathered together the second time, then Mordecai sat in the king’s gate. 20 Esther had not yet shewed her kindred nor her people; as Mordecai had charged her: for Esther did the commandment of Mordecai, like as when she was brought up with him.

2.6.1.en: When Xerxes returned defeated from his campaign against Greece, he busied himself with choosing the new queen, and it seems that what was done by way of preparations with the virgins took place before his coming from the battle and not after his coming, since the virgins remained a whole year preparing for the meeting with the king. And the book relates to us the preparations that were made for Esther, which are:

2.6.2.en: First: the days of her purification were completed, “six months with oil of myrrh, and six months with sweet odours, and with other things for the purifying of the women” [12]. What do the six months in which she was perfumed with oil of myrrh mean if not her acceptance of burial with her Bridegroom Christ, who was buried after being anointed with myrrh... She remains six months, and the number 6 signifies the days of creation, that is, she remains bearing sufferings and being buried with her Bridegroom all the days of her sojourn until her spiritual perfection is completed and she meets the Lord face to face on the seventh day. And as she is buried with the Lord, so she rises with Him, for the sweet odours and the ointments signify the joyous fragrance of the resurrection. Therefore let us suffer with Him, be buried with Him, and also rise with Him! This is the way to reach the heavenly crown. As St. John Chrysostom says: [It is fitting for you that these sufferings not trouble you but rather rejoice you... Thus it is fitting for us to walk the way so that we may share with Him in glory and honor... How glorious are the sufferings! By them we are conformed to His death!].

2.7.0.en: Second: “whatsoever she desired was given her to go with her out of the house of the women unto the king’s house” [13]. The virgin carries with her all that she wants from the house of the women (the virgins), for as she sets out to her Bridegroom the heavenly King, she carries what she has gathered here of holy things such as love, purity and heavenly thought. She carries it as a sign of love for her Bridegroom, from what He Himself gave her during the days of her sojourn on earth, that is, she offers to Him from what He gave her.

2.8.0.en: Third: “Esther obtained favour in the sight of all them that looked upon her” [15]. This is her true asset: the free grace of God, which raises the soul and lifts her until she is fit for a kingdom (Ezek 16:13), so that she finds favour in the eyes of all... This is the grace of God that upholds man in his striving, of which St. John Chrysostom said: [None is stronger than he who enjoys heavenly help, as none is weaker than he who is deprived of it].

2.9.0.en: Fourth: “Esther was taken... in the tenth month, which is the month Tebeth, in the seventh year of his reign” [16]. Esther could be set up as queen only in the tenth month in the seventh year. The tenth month signifies the fulfillment of the Law (10 commandments), which is accomplished through our union in Christ, who alone did not break the Law, while the seventh year signifies the perfection of the Gospel. It is as though our enjoyment of the Kingdom is realized by our receiving the Law spiritually in the Lord through the grace of the Gospel.

2.10.0.en: Fifth: “Then the king made a great feast unto all his princes and his servants, even Esther’s feast; and he made a release to the provinces, and gave gifts, according to the state of the king” [18]. Esther made him forget the troubles of his battle with Greece and his heavy loss, and his life was turned into joy, as he gave rest to the land, that is, exemption from tribute for a year or exemption from conscription...

2.10.1.en: The king put the crown with his own hands on her head [17], for the soul cannot reign except through Christ Jesus, who crowns her with the crown of His glory, and makes a feast in her name that gladdens the heart of the heavenly ones. And it is a rest, for the Lord counts her crown a blessed Sabbath and a joyous feast. As for His gifts, which are according to the king’s generosity, they are the giving of Himself to us as a Bridegroom whom we carry within us. He is the Giver and the gift; He does not withhold Himself from us but with joy receives us, that we may say: “My beloved is mine, and I am his: he feedeth among the lilies” (Song 2:16). And as St. Augustine addresses Him, saying: [You watch over me, as though You had forgotten all creation! You give me Your gifts, as if I alone were the object of Your love].

2.11.0.en: 21 In those days, while Mordecai sat in the king’s gate, two of the king’s chamberlains, Bigthan and Teresh, of those which kept the door, were wroth, and sought to lay hand on the king Ahasuerus. 22 And the thing was known to Mordecai, who told it unto Esther the queen; and Esther certified the king thereof in Mordecai’s name. 23 And when inquisition was made of the matter, it was found out; therefore they were both hanged on a tree: and it was written in the book of the chronicles before the king.

2.11.1.en: Mordecai was marked by faithfulness. He was faithful in his private life, as in his raising of Esther, and in his service to the king, as in his love for his people.

2.11.2.en: Mordecai learned that two chamberlains, keepers of the door, were plotting to assassinate the king, so he told Esther, who told the king. And when the king examined the matter and verified it, he hanged them on a tree, and the matter was written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of the Persians.

2.11.3.en: In (the Additions to Esth 12:4-5) it relates to us that the king gave gifts to Mordecai, but afterwards, when sleep fled from the king and he read what had been written earlier, he counted what Mordecai had received as nothing (Esth 6:1-11), and wanted to honor him in an extraordinary way. We also, when we strive here for the salvation of our brethren from eternal punishment, the Lord counts it as a debt, although He is the One working in us and with us, and so grants us blessings and graces; but all this He counts as nothing when He crowns us with the crown of eternal life and brings us into the fellowship of His glories, to live with Him face to face in the bosom of the Father.
